note: Tavern keeper, three-quarter view facing image-left, holding a grey tankard out in the left (image-left) hand. Head is the brown hair, ear and full beard, bottom y~448 at the beard tip; the cream collar, shirt, belt, apron and the purple cloth hanging at the right hip are torso. The tankard is equipment: the grey body (x316-414, y490-622) plus the two handle bars (y500-521 and y574-596) that the fingers pass through, kept off the fingers. Left arm is almost fully hidden behind the tankard: only the blue sleeve shoulder showing above it (x394-432, y448-498) is labelled upper arm (the elbow is hidden, so no forearm) and the peach and brown fingers on the handle (x266-318, y515-590) are the hand. Right arm: the big blue puffed sleeve is the upper arm to the elbow y~546 where the bare forearm emerges; the bare forearm (y545-650) and the brown and cream wrist bands (y655-712) are forearm; the brown glove fist with fingertips is the hand (y708-800). The hip is the apron hem y~800; the bare skin below is thigh to the boot tops (left y~843, right y~848), where the knees are; boots are lower leg to the ankles (left y~870, right y~893), boot toes are feet.
